origins.name: Archive child
origins.background: You grew up in the Nexus stacks, among catalogues and loan slips.
origins.link: You know how catalogues work: who files a thing, and under what name, shapes what people can find.

origins.name: Harbour runner
origins.background: You carried messages between the harbours of the coast.
origins.link: You know that a story changes as it travels from person to person.

origins.name: Workshop apprentice
origins.background: You trained with makers, and you test ideas with your hands.
origins.link: You test an idea by building it and watching what happens.

origins.name: Village singer
origins.background: You learned the songs of a valley, and the people who keep them.
origins.link: You know that songs and stories can hold knowledge for a long time.

origins.name: Traveller
origins.background: You moved between many places and many languages.
origins.link: You see a thing from more than one side, because you have stood on more than one side.

journal.text: Lens hint (Archive child): a catalogue entry has its own date. Check if a date tells when a thing was made, or only when someone wrote it down.
Lens hint (Harbour runner): when a claim reaches you through many people, ask who told the first of them.
Lens hint (Workshop apprentice): an object that works today shows what it can do. It does not show who made the first one.
Lens hint (Village singer): a song can keep knowledge for generations. Ask who sings it, and what it was made to remember.
Lens hint (Traveller): the same word can claim different things in different places. Ask what each place means by it.

dialogue.speaker: warden-ise
dialogue.text: The cataloguers do, and their choices last for centuries. A pen filed under 'inventions of 1888' is easy to find as a first. A pen filed under 'unfinished patents' is not. Shelves make claims too.

dialogue.speaker: warden-ise
dialogue.text: Yes. A visitor reads it, tells a friend, and the friend tells a class. Each copy drops a word. That is why a short, exact label matters more than a clever one.

dialogue.speaker: warden-ise
dialogue.text: You can. Read it to someone who has not seen the exhibits, then ask what they believe. If they repeat more than the label supports, the label is too strong.

dialogue.speaker: warden-ise
dialogue.text: Some. Not enough. We keep paper well and songs badly, so our shelves say more about writers than about singers. Remember that when a record is silent.

dialogue.speaker: warden-ise
dialogue.text: That is most of it. A lawyer's first, a shopkeeper's first and an engineer's first are three different claims. You will be good at this work.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: Collectors, mostly, a long time ago. Their words, 'Damascus' and 'ancient', are still on the cards. A catalogue is a record, and it is also a point of view.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: Then the story got here before the blade's maker did. Ask who started it, and who gains if people believe it.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: Then Hesper is your teacher, not me. Her anvil will show you more than my catalogue. Come back and tell me what the steel showed you.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: Some lines are almost the same: watch the hands, not the shine. Songs travel like steel does. When two places keep the same line, it is worth asking why.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: Many places have their own name for it. A name tells you who was talking, and to whom. It does not tell you where the steel was made.
